page: OVHcloud c3-8 is a compute-optimized virtual server instance running on the KVM hypervisor. It features 4 dedicated physical cores on an x86_64 AMD EPYC processor running at 2.3 GHz, with one thread per core. The hardware configuration includes 8.0 GB of system memory, providing 2.0 GB of RAM per core, along with 100 GB of local NVMe SSD storage. The CPU is equipped with a 32 KB L1d cache, 0.5 MB L2 cache, and 32 MB L3 cache, and supports AVX, AES, and SHA_NI instruction sets.

Benchmark results show strong single-core CPU performance, with stress-ng single-core scoring 3076.85 and Geekbench text processing scoring 2601.0, both placing in the top 25%. Multi-core performance is average, with a stress-ng multi-core score of 12235.05 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 6021.0. Memory performance is a notable bottleneck, as the Passmark memory score of 1832.39 falls into the bottom 25%, and static web serving throughput is also weak at 4.61 GB/sec. Large block memory bandwidth reads reach 98.26 GB/sec, while writes achieve 49.18 GB/sec.

Given the dedicated AMD EPYC cores and strong single-core execution, this instance is suited for compute-bound tasks such as software compilation and text processing. However, the low memory-to-vCPU ratio of 2.0 GB per core and weak memory benchmark scores make it less suitable for memory-intensive databases or large-scale web serving. It can handle light LLM inference workloads, achieving 228.6 tokens per second for text generation on a small 135M model, but performance drops significantly to 21.67 tokens per second for prompt processing on a medium 7B model.
